notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an average index of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice prices set at 100 in 2015, currently stands at 132, reflecting a 32% increase since that base year. This rise is primarily recent and varies significantly among the included commodities. Price movements have not been uniform, indicating differentiated pressures on each commodity rather than a broad-based trend. The index is sourced from global commodity data compiled by FRED and IMF.
notes.movers: Coffee has experienced the most substantial price increase, up 93% since 2015, followed by orange juice at 22%, wheat at 7%, and sugar at 5%. These shifts are largely due to factors such as adverse weather events and crop diseases, including frost and drought affecting arabica coffee regions and citrus greening along with hurricanes impacting orange juice. Soft commodities like these trade in relatively thin markets, where supply shocks can cause pronounced price volatility. This underscores that the price changes reflect specific commodity challenges rather than broad global inflationary forces.
notes.why: The headline rise in the basket is primarily driven by a few weather-sensitive crops subject to periodic supply disruptions. Given the nature of these agricultural risks, input costs for these commodities may remain elevated over an extended period, influencing price stability in the breakfast basket.
